## Motivation

Add FlashInfer support for zigzag prefill context parallelism on dense MHA/GQA models, addressing #21788.

## Modifications

- Add FlashInfer CP dispatch and CP-aware paged prefill metadata/execution.
- Gather full KV while keeping queries zigzag-sharded; support eager dense causal MHA/GQA with direct NHD KV.
- Use current runtime configuration without deprecated `enable_cp_v2` or model-file changes; add CPU routing/padding coverage and a Qwen3-8B `GSM8KMixin` test.

## Accuracy Result

Qwen3-8B BF16 on 2× H100. Parity compares TP2/CP2 with both cold cache and prefix reuse.

| Validation | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Registered CP2 GSM8K, 200 examples | 191/200 = **95.5%**, above the 90% floor; zero errors/truncations | Pass |
| 2K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **1.19e-7 < 0.2** | Pass |
| 8K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **0.111686 < 0.2** | Pass |
| 16K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **0 < 0.2** | Pass |

[Accuracy and current performance details](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33226#issuecomment-6101828491) · [Historical performance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33226#issuecomment-5574927639)

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with repository tools.
- [x] Add CPU unit and registered two-GPU accuracy coverage.
- [x] Provide correctness and scoped performance measurements.
- [x] Follow repository coding-style guidance.

@wirybeaver I independently reran the **unchanged current head `dd8be79c9b754bb8dd3c972617ff49a5b8bfadee`** on 2× NVIDIA L20:

- `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py`: **24 passed, 18 subtests passed, zero skips**.
- `test/registered/cp/test_flashinfer_prefill_cp.py`: **2 passed, zero skips**, JUnit duration 253.728 s. This uses the two test methods collected from the current head, not the older five-test count in the PR body.

The GPU run exercised the original MHA/GQA FA2+KV-write assertions and actual Qwen3-0.6B TP2/CP2 server output/logprob parity. After cache flush and a prefix request, the CP logs show 64 cached tokens; cold/cached parity passed. All upstream tolerances/assertions were retained; no collective or kernel replacements and no test retries.

Environment: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, FlashInfer 0.6.17, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, Transformers 5.12.1. A private venv installed your declared dependencies; `pip check` passed. Tests ran offline; optional Rust extensions were disabled with the documented build flag (HTTP/FlashInfer path only). Complete logs retain transient cold-JIT startup health/freezegc errors; the tests subsequently passed. This is correctness qualification, not a speedup or warning-free-startup claim.

Could I help with a bounded current-main/CI compatibility-validation slice on this PR, if that is useful and unclaimed? I'd coordinate the exact next head/blocker with you; no parallel CP implementation, author-branch edits, or new PR. This independent validation and coordination note were AI-assisted.

@wirybeaver I requalified the unchanged head `afe9df7b28ccfa87a4b20fcda1064f71b682221f` and found a startup blocker after the rebase:

- The 27 strategy tests + 18 subtests pass, with zero failures/errors/skips, in a GPU-inaccessible container.
- The current single GPU test, `TestFlashInferPrefillCPServer.test_qwen3_matches_tp_and_reuses_prefix`, fails during CP server startup on 2× L20. The TP2 baseline starts and serves `/generate`; CP parity/cache assertions are not reached.

Both CP scheduler ranks report this exception before any unrelated workload appeared on the selected GPUs:

```text
flashinfer_backend.py:558, _validate_prefill_cp_configuration
    and server_args.cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend == Backend.DISABLED
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'prefill'
```

The retained test passes `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`. Source inspection suggests this check still reads the raw `ServerArgs` field: `declare_resolution()` now records resolved values without writing those fields, and `ServerArgs.cuda_graph_config` defaults to `None`. The same backend already imports/uses `check_cuda_graph_backend`, which reads the published `get_exec().graph` configuration. That looks like the relevant compatibility seam to check, rather than relaxing the eager-only requirement. I have not modified or validated a fix.

Exact declared environment: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, Transformers 5.12.1; `pip check` passes. ## Historical performance measurements — superseded source/configurations

These measurements are retained for history only. They predate the current rebase/runtime changes and the Qwen3-8B test configuration; they must not be interpreted as performance of current head `9c8558beaadc9bf0bb4591be753d745436e1b0e6`.

### Original RTX 4090 results moved from the PR description

The original description did not record the exact source SHA for this run. Its CP command included the now-deprecated CP-v2 environment flag and the old replicated-MLP configuration. The results and isolated kernel profile below are preserved as originally reported; they were not rerun on the current source.

Environment:

- 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
- Driver 580.95.05
- Ubuntu 22.04.5
- CUDA 13.0.1
- FlashInfer attention, Qwen3-0.6B, batch size 1, output length 1
- Five measured samples per mode and input length

CP command additionally used `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1 --attn-cp-size 2 --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`.

| Input tokens | TP2 mean latency | CP2 mean latency | TP2 throughput | CP2 throughput | CP speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 70.75 ms | 47.16 ms | 28,959 tok/s | 43,512 tok/s | **1.50×** |
| 8,192 | 282.40 ms | 194.41 ms | 29,009 tok/s | 42,139 tok/s | **1.45×** |

<details>
<summary>Nsight Compute result</summary>

A replay-safe, Qwen-shaped FlashInfer attention invocation was profiled with Nsight Compute 2025.3.1 using container-only `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` (not privileged mode).

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Attention kernel duration | 54.53 µs |
| SM throughput | 30.01% peak |
| DRAM throughput | 11.84% peak |
| Tensor pipeline activity | 30.01% peak |
| Achieved / theoretical occupancy | 14.35% / 16.67% |
| Registers per thread | 245 |
| Shared memory per block | 50,256 bytes |
| L1 / L2 sector hit rate | 1.98% / 88.46% |

NCU classified the kernel as latency/occupancy limited rather than DRAM-bandwidth limited. Register and shared-memory pressure limit residency, while NCU also identified math-pipe throttling, workload imbalance, and inefficient global-load sector utilization. These findings concern the upstream FlashInfer kernel; the end-to-end SGLang path already shows the speedups above.

A direct distributed NCU replay was not used for conclusions because replay pauses one rank while another waits in NCCL collectives. The focused profile isolates the attention kernel and avoids that replay artifact.

</details>

### L40S validation on September 7, 2026 — original report retained

The report below refers to historical commit `7602fbeb928ab4991d320056c58f69012bb28698`, not today's head. Its reference to the RTX 4090 results in the PR summary now refers to the preceding historical section.

Reran the current head `7602fbeb928ab4991d320056c58f69012bb28698` on September 7, 2026, after the resolved-prefill-config fix.

## Accuracy and performance validation — Qwen3-8B / 2× H100

Detailed evidence for the PR's accuracy summary and the current performance measurements. Accuracy-run and performance-run source provenance are recorded separately below.

## Accuracy details

### Registered Qwen3-8B GSM8K test

```bash
python test/registered/e2e/cp/test_flashinfer_prefill_cp.py
```

Validated the actual registered test, including its original server fixture, `GSM8KMixin`, default `sgl_eval` dataset loader/scorer, assertions, and teardown.

- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 on Modal.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, BF16, revision `b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218`.
- CP configuration: `--tp-size 2 --attn-cp-size 2 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag --attention-backend flashinfer --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`.
- Thinking disabled through `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`.
- 200 examples, 8 threads, maximum 1,024 output tokens; configured accuracy floor: 0.90.
- Result: **191/200 = 95.5%; 1 test passed** (`Ran 1 test in 167.328s; OK`).
- Errors, truncations, and invalid answers: **0**.

Source provenance: runtime commit `25f1cea48db47fb243732a638885c5d3101e4c5b` plus the exact test overlay subsequently committed as `9c8558beaadc9bf0bb4591be753d745436e1b0e6`. The tested file SHA256 matches the committed file: `9472329724f28ab8fe5427c5a2bca75793e6cc2744d174dfa3ef17358e19480d`. That commit changes only the test configuration, not runtime code.

### Focused TP2/CP2 cold-cache and prefix-reuse consistency experiment

Separately validated the same Qwen3-8B revision on 2× H100 at runtime commit `25f1cea48db47fb243732a638885c5d3101e4c5b`. These are additional GPU experiment results, not extra cases in the registered GSM8K test.

For each input length, compared all four responses: TP2 cold, TP2 prefix reuse, CP2 cold, and CP2 prefix reuse. Requests used temperature 0, sampling seed 0, and 4 generated tokens. Prefix reuse primed 75% of the input; the prime's generated tokens were also retained in the cache.

| Input tokens | Output token IDs across all four responses | Maximum absolute generated-token logprob delta, all pairs | Cold cached tokens | Reuse cached tokens, both arms |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | Identical | 0.0000001192 | 0 | 1,540 |
| 8,192 | Identical | 0.1116856933 | 0 | 6,148 |
| 16,384 | Identical | 0 | 0 | 12,292 |

**All comparisons passed the predeclared absolute logprob tolerance of 0.2.** This is focused generated-token parity evidence, not a claim of bitwise-equivalent logits or identical answers on all prompts.

A separate paired 200-example GSM8K experiment on that runtime also scored TP2 192/200 (96.0%) and CP2 191/200 (95.5%), with matching example IDs and prompt hashes and zero errors/truncations.

### Reproducibility and local checks

- Digest-pinned image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:767b19a009270ef21849719fa3146143035d47a4f302429fb3d26bb98d141466`.
- Torch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1; sglang-kernel 0.4.9; transformers 5.19.0; sgl-eval 0.1.2.
- Explicit `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python` for all server processes.
- CPU tests, isort, Ruff lint/format, and registered-test checks passed locally.
- GPU reports/logs were persisted to Modal Volumes, downloaded, and SHA256-verified; owned Sandboxes were terminated with zero tasks/containers.
- These are local/Modal validation results, not a claim that GitHub Actions GPU CI has passed.

## Performance details — 2× H100 / Qwen3-8B (October 10, 2026)

Tested source `9c8558beaadc9bf0bb4591be753d745436e1b0e6`, with source archive SHA256 `338d2d6c60d5678b9a41dc1fa805ebfea8df23912cf16f0f84dd215abd287185`.

**Result: CP2 had higher mean latency than TP2 in all six tested workloads. No speedup is claimed for this configuration.** These results do not replace the historical hardware/model results with a like-for-like regression comparison.

### Locked environment and workloads

- Modal Sandbox; 2× NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; MIG disabled; same physical GPU UUIDs across all six visits.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, revision `b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218`; BF16.
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:767b19a009270ef21849719fa3146143035d47a4f302429fb3d26bb98d141466`.
- Driver 580.95.05; Torch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1; sglang-kernel 0.4.9; transformers 5.19.0.
- Both arms: FlashInfer, `--tp-size 2 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --context-length 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.70`.
- CP2 additionally: `--attn-cp-size 2 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`. This is two GPUs total, not TP2 × CP2 on four GPUs.
- Resolved chunked prefill size: 8,192; max prefill tokens: 16,384, identical across all visits.
- Explicit Python TreeCore backend in both arms: `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python`.
- Fixed disjoint affinity: server CPUs 11–22, client CPUs 23–26; identical across visits.
- Concurrency 1, one output token, temperature 0, `sampling_seed=0`, `ignore_eos=true`.
- Fixed deterministic synthetic token-ID cohorts and prompt hashes, identical across arms/visits.
- Cold requests were flushed individually and all reported 0 cached tokens.
- Each reuse leg was reset and primed once with a 75% prefix; distinct suffixes avoided accidental full-prompt hits. Actual cached tokens were exactly 1,536 / 6,144 / 12,288 for 2K / 8K / 16K inputs.

### Schedule and measurement

One live server at a time, ordered visits **TP2 → CP2 → CP2 → TP2 → TP2 → CP2**. Every visit used a fresh server, including adjacent equal arms, with owned-process/port/GPU-memory release checks.

Each startup received 32 cold-cache 16K substantial warmup requests. Each workload then had 8 shape warmups immediately followed by 256 timed samples. This gives **768 timed samples per arm per workload**, 36 timed legs and **9,216 timed samples** overall.

Persistent HTTP session with retries disabled. The primary metric is caller-side **non-streaming single-output completion latency, a TTFT proxy rather than exact streamed TTFT**. Flush and prefix-prime operations were outside the measured interval. Every sample, including outliers, was retained.

| Cache | Input tokens | TP2 mean (ms) | CP2 mean (ms) | TP2 P95 (ms) | CP2 P95 (ms) | CP2 mean latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold | 2,048 | 42.07 | 63.40 | 62.28 | 94.25 | +50.7% |
| Cold | 8,192 | 145.11 | 162.16 | 176.38 | 195.45 | +11.7% |
| Cold | 16,384 | 345.40 | 378.87 | 373.27 | 410.09 | +9.7% |
| 75% prefix reuse | 2,048 | 44.43 | 56.55 | 48.67 | 59.99 | +27.3% |
| 75% prefix reuse | 8,192 | 49.55 | 57.95 | 50.40 | 62.20 | +16.9% |
| 75% prefix reuse | 16,384 | 116.88 | 122.91 | 118.53 | 124.34 | +5.2% |

<details>
<summary>P50, maximum latency, and actual processed-input throughput</summary>

Throughput is actual processed input tokens (`input_tokens - cached_tokens`) divided by summed caller generation latency. It is not end-to-end leg throughput including cache preparation.

| Workload | Arm | P50 (ms) | Max (ms) | Processed input tok/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold_2048 | TP2 | 39.78 | 92.91 | 48,683 |
| cold_2048 | CP2 | 59.80 | 132.67 | 32,305 |
| cold_8192 | TP2 | 141.48 | 234.39 | 56,454 |
| cold_8192 | CP2 | 158.16 | 251.91 | 50,518 |
| cold_16384 | TP2 | 340.50 | 433.87 | 47,435 |
| cold_16384 | CP2 | 371.97 | 476.52 | 43,245 |
| reuse_2048 | TP2 | 44.09 | 71.61 | 11,523 |
| reuse_2048 | CP2 | 56.46 | 61.65 | 9,053 |
| reuse_8192 | TP2 | 49.52 | 56.67 | 41,333 |
| reuse_8192 | CP2 | 57.87 | 95.53 | 35,343 |
| reuse_16384 | TP2 | 116.78 | 128.98 | 35,045 |
| reuse_16384 | CP2 | 122.85 | 127.88 | 33,325 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Three matched-visit mean-latency speedup ratios</summary>

Speedup = TP2 mean / CP2 mean; below 1 means CP2 is slower. Pairs are visits (1 TP2, 2 CP2), (4 TP2, 3 CP2), and (5 TP2, 6 CP2).

| Workload | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Pair 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold_2048 | 0.6937× | 0.6331× | 0.6655× |
| cold_8192 | 0.8918× | 0.9026× | 0.8902× |
| cold_16384 | 0.9079× | 0.9123× | 0.9148× |
| reuse_2048 | 0.8035× | 0.8206× | 0.7357× |
| reuse_8192 | 0.8434× | 0.8856× | 0.8378× |
| reuse_16384 | 0.9487× | 0.9539× | 0.9501× |

</details>

### Scope and evidence

- All **9,714 generation requests** (including warmups/primes) and **4,962 flushes** completed successfully; zero failed or filtered samples.
- No independent A/A noise calibration was run in this single-server restart schedule; small differences are not presented as noise-calibrated conclusions.
- No profiler was run and no specific bottleneck/root cause is claimed.
- No TP1 baseline was measured; these numbers cannot establish scaling relative to one GPU or behavior outside the tested workloads.
- Each startup emitted a caught, nonfatal `freeze_gc` warning; all readiness and workload gates passed.
- Manifest SHA256: `9ff09c844c84e5513d75484de8452b813880bc82bb79b086745ece42d1853880`.
- Durable evidence: Modal Volume v1 `fi-cp-perf-9c8558beaa-iUHqF6`, directory `flashinfer-cp-perf-9c8558beaa-iUHqF6`; includes immutable manifest/cohort fingerprints, raw `requests.jsonl`, all 36 leg summaries, launch/readiness/cleanup records and checksums.
- All 70 required artifacts were downloaded and independently SHA256-verified. Sandbox terminated immediately after execution; zero owned tasks/containers. Allocation wall time: 1800.614 seconds (~30 minutes).
The modification under `models` folder looks unrelated to Prefill CP. Can we remove them?

@wirybeaver I requalified the unchanged head `afe9df7b28ccfa87a4b20fcda1064f71b682221f` and found a startup blocker after the rebase:

AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'prefill'

The same backend already imports/uses `check_cuda_graph_backend`, which reads the published `get_exec().graph` configuration. That looks like the relevant compatibility seam to check, rather than relaxing the eager-only requirement. I have not modified or validated a fix.

These measurements are retained for history only. They predate the current rebase/runtime changes and the Qwen3-8B test configuration; they must not be interpreted as performance of current head `9c8558beaadc9bf0bb4591be753d745436e1b0e6`.

### Original RTX 4090 results moved from the PR description

The original description did not record the exact source SHA for this run. Its CP command included the now-deprecated CP-v2 environment flag and the old replicated-MLP configuration. | 8,192 | 282.40 ms | 194.41 ms | 29,009 tok/s | 42,139 tok/s | **1.45×** |

<details>
<summary>Nsight Compute result</summary>

A replay-safe, Qwen-shaped FlashInfer attention invocation was profiled with Nsight Compute 2025.3.1 using container-only `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` (not privileged mode).

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Attention kernel duration | 54.53 µs |
| SM throughput | 30.01% peak |
| DRAM throughput | 11.84% peak |
| Tensor pipeline activity | 30.01% peak |
| Achieved / theoretical occupancy | 14.35% / 16.67% |
| Registers per thread | 245 |
| Shared memory per block | 50,256 bytes |
| L1 / L2 sector hit rate | 1.98% / 88.46% |

NCU classified the kernel as latency/occupancy limited rather than DRAM-bandwidth limited. Register and shared-memory pressure limit residency, while NCU also identified math-pipe throttling, workload imbalance, and inefficient global-load sector utilization. These findings concern the upstream FlashInfer kernel; the end-to-end SGLang path already shows the speedups above.

A direct distributed NCU replay was not used for conclusions because replay pauses one rank while another waits in NCCL collectives. The focused profile isolates the attention kernel and avoids that replay artifact.

</details>

## Performance details — 2× H100 / Qwen3-8B (October 10, 2026)

Tested source `9c8558beaadc9bf0bb4591be753d745436e1b0e6`, with source archive SHA256 `338d2d6c60d5678b9a41dc1fa805ebfea8df23912cf16f0f84dd215abd287185`.

**Result: CP2 had higher mean latency than TP2 in all six tested workloads. No speedup is claimed for this configuration.** These results do not replace the historical hardware/model results with a like-for-like regression comparison.

### Locked environment and workloads

- Modal Sandbox; 2× NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; MIG disabled; same physical GPU UUIDs across all six visits.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, revision `b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218`; BF16.
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:767b19a009270ef21849719fa3146143035d47a4f302429fb3d26bb98d141466`.
- Driver 580.95.05; Torch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1; sglang-kernel 0.4.9; transformers 5.19.0.
- Both arms: FlashInfer, `--tp-size 2 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --context-length 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.70`.
- CP2 additionally: `--attn-cp-size 2 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`. This is two GPUs total, not TP2 × CP2 on four GPUs.
- Resolved chunked prefill size: 8,192; max prefill tokens: 16,384, identical across all visits.
- Explicit Python TreeCore backend in both arms: `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python`.
- Fixed disjoint affinity: server CPUs 11–22, client CPUs 23–26; identical across visits.
- Concurrency 1, one output token, temperature 0, `sampling_seed=0`, `ignore_eos=true`.
- Fixed deterministic synthetic token-ID cohorts and prompt hashes, identical across arms/visits.
- Cold requests were flushed individually and all reported 0 cached tokens.
- Each reuse leg was reset and primed once with a 75% prefix; distinct suffixes avoided accidental full-prompt hits. Actual cached tokens were exactly 1,536 / 6,144 / 12,288 for 2K / 8K / 16K inputs.

### Schedule and measurement

One live server at a time, ordered visits **TP2 → CP2 → CP2 → TP2 → TP2 → CP2**. Every visit used a fresh server, including adjacent equal arms, with owned-process/port/GPU-memory release checks.

Each startup received 32 cold-cache 16K substantial warmup requests. Each workload then had 8 shape warmups immediately followed by 256 timed samples. This gives **768 timed samples per arm per workload**, 36 timed legs and **9,216 timed samples** overall.

Persistent HTTP session with retries disabled. The primary metric is caller-side **non-streaming single-output completion latency, a TTFT proxy rather than exact streamed TTFT**. Flush and prefix-prime operations were outside the measured interval. Every sample, including outliers, was retained.
